My Big Tracing Day  ·  Little Worlds Learning
3: Little hands are just getting ready to write. This book builds the first skills step by step: big lines, shapes, paths, then numbers and letters when your child is ready.

•  Start at the green dot and follow the arrow.
•  Trace with a finger first, then with a crayon.
•  One or two pages a day is plenty – stop while it's still fun.
•  Go back to favourite pages any time.

•  Chunky crayons are easiest for little hands.
•  A whole-hand grip is normal at 2; a finger grip comes later.
•  Let your child choose either hand.
•  Sit at a table with feet supported if you can.

•  Wobbly lines are perfect – they are learning!
•  Praise trying: “You followed the dots all the way!”
•  Colour the star at the top of each page together.
•  Name the pictures and talk about them.

•  Use crayons or pencils – markers can bleed through the paper.
•  Printing at home? Print at Actual size; single-sided is best.
•  Always supervise young children with crayons and pencils.
•  Lamination plus a dry-erase crayon makes pages reusable.
